answer: A backdoor works by allowing an adversary to gain unauthorized access to a system after the malicious software has been deployed. This is typically achieved by designing malware that creates a hidden entry point into the system, which can be exploited for further attacks or to disrupt operations. The backdoor remains undetected, enabling the attacker to execute additional malicious actions once the system is compromised [Source 2].
